native_result.query: Between which two races is the factor of BA degree completion -0.9568 when compared to the other?
native_result.HypoA: There is a racial differential in BA degree completion rates between Black and White students with a factor of -0.9568.
native_result.HypoB: The factor of -0.9568 for BA degree completion is observed between Hispanic and White respondents, where Hispanic respondents have lower BA-completion odds than White (negative log-odds factor); Black vs White is the runner-up (-1.0057). The exact value is not reproduced by any standard specification on the processed data (closest two-race matches are -0.9241 Hispanic-White and -1.0057 Black-White, which bracket -0.9568).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inspected data (n=8773, no missingness; White 5337, Black 2113, Hispanic 1323; BA rate 2.69% overall, White 3.54%, Black 1.33%, Hispanic 1.44%). 2) Modeled BA degree completion as outcome via logistic regression with race as categorical factor (treatment coding, each reference in turn) plus exhaustive covariate-subset/link search (logit/probit/log/cloglog, OLS, both model directions, subgroup splits). 3) Applied approved rule: nearest two-race log-odds coefficient to -0.9568 with negative sign -> Hispanic vs White (-0.9241, |d|=0.033) over Black vs White (-1.0057, |d|=0.049); Black-Hispanic negligible (+0.08) excludes it. 4) Recorded the limitation that -0.9568 is not exactly reproduced and lies between the two White-vs-minority coefficients.
